schema_sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workload_table (id INT PRIMARY KEY, category VARCHAR(64), payload NVARCHAR(MAX), created_at DATETIME)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reference_table (id INT PRIMARY KEY, status INT, description NVARCHAR(255))
generation_sql: INSERT INTO reference_table (id, status, description) SELECT n, n % 5, CONCAT('Description_', n) FROM (SELECT TOP 1000 ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT NULL)) AS n FROM sys.objects) AS numbers

INSERT INTO workload_table (id, category, payload, created_at) SELECT n, CASE WHEN n % 100 = 0 THEN 'high_memory' ELSE 'normal' END, REPLICATE('X', 1000), GETDATE() FROM (SELECT TOP {row_count} ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT NULL)) AS n FROM sys.objects) AS numbers

calibration_queries.sql: SELECT TOP 10 * FROM workload_table WHERE category = 'high_memory' ORDER BY created_at DESC
calibration_queries.objective: Verify that the data distribution and indexes support the intended query behavior.
expected_evidence: The query plan shows a scan or seek operation on the workload_table.
The predicate on category is applied efficiently.

calibration_queries.sql: SELECT w.* FROM workload_table w JOIN reference_table r ON w.id = r.id WHERE w.category = 'high_memory'
calibration_queries.objective: Verify join behavior and memory grant requirements.
expected_evidence: The query plan shows a join operation with memory grants.
The join behavior reflects the intended one-to-one relationship.
